payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer m >= 2 and a tuple x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers satisfying the stated Kunz inequalities, and define

S_x = {0} ∪ {q m : q ∈ N0} ∪ {q m + (m x_i + i) : q ∈ N0, 1 <= i <= m-1}.

We must prove that the genus g(S_x), i.e. the number of elements of N0 \ S_x, is

sum_{i=1}^{m-1} x_i.

The proof is by describing exactly which nonnegative integers are missing from S_x.

First, every nonnegative integer n has a unique expression n = q m + r with q ∈ N0 and 0 <= r <= m-1.

We analyze membership in S_x residue class by residue class modulo m.

1. Residue class 0 modulo m.
If r=0, then n=q m, so by definition n ∈ S_x. Hence there are no gaps in the residue class 0 modulo m.

2. Residue class i modulo m, where 1 <= i <= m-1.
Take n = q m + i with q ∈ N0.

We claim:

n ∈ S_x if and only if q >= x_i.

Indeed, by definition, the elements of S_x congruent to i mod m are exactly those of the form

q' m + (m x_i + i) = (q' + x_i)m + i

with q' ∈ N0. Thus the set of elements of S_x having residue i mod m is exactly

{t m + i : t >= x_i, t ∈ N0}.

So for n=q m+i we have n ∈ S_x exactly when q >= x_i, proving the claim.

Therefore the elements of N0 in residue class i that are not in S_x are precisely

i, m+i, 2m+i, ..., (x_i-1)m+i.

Because x_i is a positive integer, this list contains exactly x_i numbers.

3. Counting all gaps.
By the preceding analysis, the gaps of S_x are exactly the union over i=1,...,m-1 of the sets

{i, m+i, 2m+i, ..., (x_i-1)m+i}.

These sets are pairwise disjoint, because their elements have different residues modulo m. Hence the total number of gaps is the sum of their cardinalities:

|N0 \ S_x| = sum_{i=1}^{m-1} x_i.

By definition of genus, g(S_x) = |N0 \ S_x|. Therefore

g(S_x) = sum_{i=1}^{m-1} x_i.

This is exactly the desired conclusion.

Note that the Kunz inequalities were not needed for this counting argument itself; they serve to ensure that the set defined from x is indeed a numerical semigroup in the intended correspondence. Once S_x is given by the displayed formula, the genus is determined by the above residue-class count.

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2, and let x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) be a tuple of positive integers satisfying the Kunz inequalities: for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}. Define S_x = {0} union {q m : q in N0} union {q m + (m x_i + i) : q in N0 and 1 <= i <= m-1}. Then the genus of the numerical semigroup S_x is exactly x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_{m-1}.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly characterizes membership in S_x in each residue class modulo m.
The argument that the gaps are exactly the listed finite sets and are pairwise disjoint is correct and sufficient to compute the genus.
There is no substantive semantic drift: the lemma proved matches the stated genus formula and aligns with the root theorem's Kunz-coordinate framework.

result_payload.reason: The proof gives a complete residue-class analysis of the set S_x. For residue 0, all multiples of m are in S_x. For each residue i in {1,...,m-1}, it correctly identifies the elements of S_x with that residue as exactly {t m + i : t >= x_i}, so the missing elements in that residue class are exactly i, m+i, ..., (x_i-1)m+i, numbering x_i many. These gap sets are disjoint by residue class, and summing their sizes gives the genus. The note that Kunz inequalities are not used in the counting argument is semantically acceptable: they are only needed to ensure S_x is a numerical semigroup in the broader correspondence.
